deep.reconstruction:
This page has no handwritten text apart from the folio number '143'. It is scrap computer paper: an upside-down CRAY2/JES2 job banner dated 19 Aug 82. On it are pencil and ink sketches of local configurations of lines or pseudo-lines.

(1) Upper left: two marked points joined by a thick segment. A long line passes through both. Other lines cross each point transversally. A red dashed curve runs along the long line but leaves it near the points. This looks like a pseudo-line that has been deformed off a 'stretched' straight line, i.e. it now passes on a chosen side of the crossings.

(2) Centre left: a smaller configuration with two marked points on a vertical line and several oblique lines.

(3) Centre: two 'stars', points where 4-5 lines meet, lying on a long nearly horizontal line ending at blobs. This is a picture of multiple (non-simple) crossing points of an arrangement.

(4) Upper right: a further star with three marked points.

(5) Lower right: two multiple points joined by a horizontal segment. A diagonal family of lines passes through them. A red dashed curve and a green dashed curve are two alternative deformed pseudo-lines that pass on different sides of the multiple points. This is the local picture of moving a pseudo-line across a vertex, or of choosing a perturbation (simplification) of a multiple crossing.

Read with the neighbouring pages, which list sequences of permutations of A..G (e.g. ABCDEFG -> ... -> GAEDCFB, with levels 1'-11 and dashed horizontal sweep lines), the page serves Grothendieck's study of 'systèmes de pseudo-droites'. Its topics are:
- encoding an arrangement by the sequence of permutations seen by a sweeping pseudo-line, i.e. an allowable sequence;
- the elementary moves that occur when a sweep line, or a pseudo-line of the arrangement, passes through a crossing point, possibly a multiple one;
- how multiple points split into simple crossings under perturbation, the two dashed choices giving different resulting permutation orders.

No statements or computations appear on this page itself.

ideas.what: Deforming a pseudo-line (red/green dashed) so it passes on one side or the other of a multiple crossing point; local moves of arrangements
ideas.modern_name: Triangle flips / mutations; Ringel homotopy (isotopy) of pseudoline arrangements; perturbation (simplification) of multiple points

ideas.what: Arrangements with multiple points seen as stars, in the context of sweeping and encoding by permutation sequences (neighbouring pages)
ideas.modern_name: Allowable sequences of permutations; topological sweep of arrangements

deep.surprise_reason: These are purely illustrative sketches of local moves in pseudo-line arrangements, with no text. The ideas visible (perturbing a pseudo-line around multiple crossings, as context for permutation sweeps) are standard in the Ringel / Goodman–Pollack theory. The only mild interest is documentary: Grothendieck worked through these local pictures himself, in 1983-84, on recycled CRAY2 printout paper.
transcription_corrections: The printed listing is upside down and reads '****A END JOB 25 CRAY2 ROOM 9.03.23 AM 19 AUG 82 R6.PR1 SYS JES2 JOB 25 END A****', repeated six times. The large banner letters spell 'CRAY2' and '0025', also printed upside down.
Handwritten '143' at bottom left is the folio number.
The dark marks resembling 'A' and '!' near the centre are ink blots, not text.
The bottom right banner line (upside down) reads roughly 'I 0025 CRAY2 ...'.
